==30%==
Charlie, Dylan, Talia and Hope play tennis doubles every Saturday. They swap pairings each week and once they have played with each of the others, they start the cycle again. What is the maximum number of times in a month that Charlie and Dylan are on the same team?

Each person has the same doubles partner once every four weeks. The maximum number of Saturdays in a month is five, so it is impossible to have the same pairings more than twice in a month.

==25%==
{| class="fandom-table"
! colspan="4" |In a parallel world where surnames are descriptive, which of these men is the oldest?
|-
| '''Jack Robertson'''
|William Jackson
|John Williamson
|Will Johnson
|}
Will is John’s son. John is William’s son. William is Jack’s son. Jack is Robert’s son, but Robert is not one of the options, so the answer must be Jack.

==20%==
How many words in this question make a new word when you put them in front of the letters which are below?

EVER

When you add ever to How, When and Which, they become However, Whenever and Whichever.

==15% ==
This list of first names is not in alphabetical order. If you can only move a name by swapping it directly with another, what is the minimum number of swaps needed to make the list alphabetical?

Ceri Sam Fiona Luna Rob Michelle Paul Deb

Ceri Deb Fiona Luna Michelle Paul Rob Sam

Swap Sam & Deb, Rob & Michelle, Rob & Paul.

== 10% ==
Your mum calls you in for dinner on a Monday at 8pm. For the rest of the week she calls you in half an hour earlier each day. On Saturday night the clocks go back an hour. What time does she call you in for dinner on Sunday?

'''5pm''': It makes no difference that the clocks go back an hour. So, 6 days x 30 minutes = 3 hours.
